name: 中国四川料理 駱駝 (Chugoku Shisen Ryori Rakuda)

claims.text: Sichuan seasonings used here (doubanjiang, sweet wheat-flour paste, soy-based sauces) typically contain wheat, and the tantanmen noodles are wheat; assume wheat throughout.
Dishes are built on pork, dried shrimp and scallop; the tantanmen mince and broths are animal-based.

name: 中華料理 鷭 (Chuka Ryori Ban)

claims.text: Town-Chinese kitchen using shared woks/pans and a single fry station, so wheat and other allergens cross freely; no gluten-free handling indicated.
Chinese-style ramen and stir-fry seasoning almost certainly use standard wheat-based shoyu/Chinese sauces; no wheat-free tare or sauce noted.
Broth, fried rice and plates are built on pork/animal fat and egg; no separate vegan preparation available.

name: 中華そば アッキー (Chuka Soba Akky)

claims.text: The bowls are built on a soy-sauce (shoyu) tare, including a dark-soy 'black' version; standard Japanese shoyu is brewed with wheat.
Every broth is a 100% pork soup with back fat and pork toppings, so there is unavoidable animal content throughout the kitchen.

name: 中華そば 尋 (Chuka Soba Hiro)

claims.text: Wheat ramen noodles are the base of every bowl and are boiled in shared water; there is no gluten-free option or separate preparation noted.
The broth is a pork-bone shoyu (豚骨醤油) tare, and soy sauce is also part of the recommended free-rice topping and the tabletop condiments — soy sauce in Japan typically contains wheat.
The single broth is animal-based (pork bone), prepared alongside chashu (pork belly) and egg toppings; no vegan preparation exists.

name: 中華そば ますたに 北白川本店 (Chuka Soba Masutani Kitashirakawa Honten)

claims.text: The broth is a chicken-bone soup combined with soy sauce (鶏ガラでとったスープに醤油を合わせた), and the soy-sauce tare in this style is virtually always wheat-based.
The signature bowl uses chicken-bone broth with pork back fat and chashu, with no plant-based version offered.

name: 中華そば みみお (Chuka Soba Mimio)

claims.text: The signature bowl is a soy-sauce-seasoned chicken-and-dashi ramen; soy sauce tare is normally wheat-based, so the broth should be assumed to contain wheat/gluten.
Broth is built on chicken bones and fish/dashi with pork-belly chashu, and pidan (egg) is a popular side - no vegan-safe preparation is offered.

name: 中華そば おにぎり ◯△ (Chuka Soba Onigiri Maru-Sankaku)

claims.text: The tare is described as aged re-brewed soy sauce from an established brewery (老舗蔵元の再仕込み熟成醤油), a wheat-based soy sauce.

Both signature broths are animal-based (domestic chicken with chicken oil; or scallop/clam/flying-fish/bonito-style seafood stock), so shared pots and water mean cross-contact with animal ingredients is inherent.

name: 中華そば 高安 (Chuka Soba Takayasu)

claims.text: Wheat ramen noodles boiled in shared water; signature broth served over wheat-kansui noodles. No gluten-free accommodation indicated.
All featured items are pork/chicken-bone broth based with pork, beef-sinew, and fried-chicken toppings; no vegan/vegetarian preparation noted.
